chunks.title: FORGE FIELD (offline field app)
chunks.heading: FORGE FIELD (offline field app)
chunks.text:
A phone-first app for Fire/EMS crews at `<department>.forgeresponder.com/field`
(or `/<department>/field` on the shared domain). It opens and saves records with
no connection and sends them automatically when the device is back online.
Department administrators customize it in the RMS under **System Admin →
FORGE FIELD (field app)**. The desktop RMS itself is unchanged.

Screenshots: [docs/field-app](field-app/).

chunks.title: FORGE FIELD (offline field app)
chunks.heading: FORGE FIELD (offline field app) — Customizing (System Admin → FORGE FIELD)
chunks.text:
- **General**: app name and logo shown in the field app's top bar.
- **Workflows**: switch each workflow on or off and choose which roles get it
  (people still need the matching permission). Pre-fire plans also have
  "Can create & edit" roles.
- **Form fields**: for each form, set fields to Show / Hide / Required for the
  whole department, and override per role (with several roles the most visible
  setting wins: Required, then Show, then Hide). Fields a record can't be saved
  without are always required and aren't listed. Truck check items come from
  Fleet → Configuration Studio, inspection items from inspection templates.
- **Check-off lists**: EMS unit and supply closet lists: items, category, par,
  unit, expiration tracking with warning days, required, order.
- **Check-off results**: recent counts with the restock list; "Mark restocked".
- **Plan updates**: updates crews sent from pre-fire plans; review, then mark
  reviewed or dismiss.

Phones pick up settings on their next data update (on open with signal, every 20
minutes, after a sync, or Update on the home screen). Settings, check-off lists and
restock marks are admin-only in Firestore rules (Fire Chief, IT Admin, Department
Admin, creators).

chunks.title: FORGE FIELD (offline field app)
chunks.heading: FORGE FIELD (offline field app) — How offline works
chunks.text:
- **App files**: a service worker (`dist/sw.js`, generated by
  `vite-plugins/fieldServiceWorker.js`) is registered for the field app's own
  address only (`/field`, `/<department>/field`), so the desktop RMS never goes
  through it. It stores the app entry, the field app's code and CSS on the first
  visit. Pages are network-first with the stored shell as fallback; hashed
  `/assets/*` are cache-first. Map tiles and plan photos viewed online are kept for
  offline use. Firestore, Auth and other sites are never intercepted.
- **Sign-in**: Firebase keeps the sign-in on the device (two-factor accounts enter
  their authenticator code). Each online start saves an access snapshot
  (department, roles, permissions, modules) in IndexedDB, so the app can open
  offline. One connected start per device is required.
- **Reference data**: FORGE FIELD settings, apparatus, published checklists,
  check-off lists, hydrants, today's hydrant activity, personnel, recent daily
  logs, NERIS drafts, assigned inspections and the violation code list, and
  pre-fire plans are downloaded to IndexedDB when online. If one part fails the
  previous copy is kept.
- **Records**: everything is saved to IndexedDB first (`src/field/fieldRecords.js`).
  New forms autosave as drafts while typing; "Pick up where you left off" on Home.
- **Plan files**: "Save offline" on a plan stores its files on the phone. PDFs need
  the storage bucket to allow browser downloads (CORS), one-time setup:

  ```bash
  gsutil cors set storage.cors.json gs://<your-storage-bucket>
  ```

  Without it, photos still show offline once viewed; PDFs open only with signal.

chunks.title: FORGE FIELD (offline field app)
chunks.heading: FORGE FIELD (offline field app) — Sync and conflict rules (`src/field/fieldSync.js`, `fieldSyncHandlers.js`)
chunks.text:
- Records send oldest first when the device is online (also on app focus and
  every 30 s). Ids are fixed on the device, so a retry overwrites instead of
  duplicating. Multi-step records (truck check, damage form, inspection, new plan)
  remember finished steps and resume.
- Connection problems: the record stays "Saved on device" and retries with
  backoff (15 s doubling to 10 min). If the phone says it's online but the server
  can't be reached, the status shows "No signal".
- The server refuses a record (permissions, plan, locked log/report, inspection
  completed in the RMS): the record is marked **Needs attention**, kept on the
  device, and can be edited and sent again, downloaded as a JSON copy, or
  discarded (with a confirmation).
- Edits to records that already exist on the server (daily logs, NERIS drafts,
  inspection answers, pre-fire plans, hydrant info) use a three-way merge per
  field: fields only the crew changed are applied; fields changed on the server
  too are shown side by side to keep mine / theirs / both. Hydrant summaries are
  only updated if the field check isn't older than the server's. Late truck checks
  don't overwrite a newer check's readiness.
- Status pill (always visible): Offline · N saved on device / Syncing N… /
  All synced / N need attention.

chunks.title: Forge AI configuration
chunks.heading: Forge AI configuration — Turning Forge AI on for a department
chunks.text:
Forge AI is **off** for every department until someone turns it on.

1. Sign in as a member with **Turn Forge AI and its capabilities on or off** (`manageForgeAi`). Fire Chief and IT Admin have it by default.
2. Open **Forge AI → Admin**, or **System Admin → Forge AI settings**.
3. Tick **Forge AI is on for this department**.
4. Untick any capability the department should not use. All capabilities are on by default once Forge AI is on.
5. Set the **daily question limit** (whole department, 1–5000, default 300). The count resets at midnight in the department's time zone.
6. Select **Save settings**. Changes apply to the next question and are recorded in the audit trail.

Turning Forge AI off stops new questions immediately. Members' conversation history is kept.

chunks.heading: Forge AI configuration — Who can use it
chunks.text: Members also need the Forge AI permissions and access to each capability's data. See [FORGE_AI_PERMISSION_MATRIX.md](FORGE_AI_PERMISSION_MATRIX.md). Forge AI never shows a member data they couldn't already open in FORGE.

chunks.title: Forge AI configuration
chunks.heading: Forge AI configuration — AI model
chunks.text:
Forge AI uses the Anthropic API key already used by the NERIS AI Narrative Writer (the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` Cloud Functions secret). There is no separate key and no key in the browser.

- Model: `claude-opus-5-5`, effort `medium`, structured JSON output.
- If the key isn't set, the model is unavailable, or its answer fails validation, Forge AI answers directly from the records instead and labels the answer **From records (no AI model)**. Forge AI shows a notice on its page when no key is configured.

chunks.title: Forge AI configuration
chunks.heading: Forge AI configuration — Usage and audit
chunks.text:
**Forge AI → Admin** (with `viewForgeAiUsage`) shows the last 30 days:

- Questions per day, split into AI-written answers, answers from records, access checks and errors, with model token counts.
- The 100 most recent questions: member, capability, answer type, outcome, number of sources and time taken. Question text is not shown here; it stays in each member's own history.
- Feedback (helpful / not helpful and comments).
- The Forge AI audit trail: every question (`forge_ai.ask`) and every settings change (`forge_ai.settings`). These entries also appear in the department audit log.

chunks.title: Forge AI configuration
chunks.heading: Forge AI configuration — Updating the knowledge base and NERIS rules
chunks.text:
Platform Knowledge answers come from a packed index of the Markdown files in `docs/`. Forge AI checks NERIS reports with the same rules as the NERIS report editor, bundled for Cloud Functions. After changing either, rebuild both before deploying:

```bash
npm run build:forge-ai
```

This writes `functions/lib/forgeAi/generated/knowledgeIndex.json` and `functions/lib/forgeAi/generated/nerisValidation.cjs`. A unit test fails if the bundled NERIS rules no longer match `src/lib/neris/validation.js`.

Specs, plans, audits and Forge AI's own design notes are left out of the index so Forge AI never describes planned work as a feature. The exclude list is at the top of `scripts/build-forge-ai-knowledge.mjs`.

chunks.title: Forge AI deployment
chunks.heading: Forge AI deployment
chunks.text: Forge AI ships as part of the normal FORGE Responder deploy. It adds Cloud Functions, Firestore rules and frontend code. It needs no new secrets and no new Firestore indexes.

chunks.title: Forge AI deployment
chunks.heading: Forge AI deployment — What changes
chunks.text:
| Part | Change |
|---|---|
| Cloud Functions | 10 new callables: `forgeAiBootstrap`, `forgeAiAsk`, `forgeAiListConversations`, `forgeAiGetConversation`, `forgeAiRenameConversation`, `forgeAiArchiveConversation`, `forgeAiFeedback`, `forgeAiGetSettings`, `forgeAiSaveSettings`, `forgeAiUsageReport` |
| Secrets | Reuses `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (already set for the NERIS AI Narrative Writer) |
| Firestore rules | 8 new department collections: owner-only reads for conversations, messages, sources and briefings; no client access to settings, usage or feedback; no client writes anywhere |
| Firestore indexes | None (all queries are single-field) |
| Roles | 5 new permissions in the default roles (see the permission matrix). Existing departments' custom roles don't get them automatically; grant them in Roles & permissions |
| Frontend | Forge AI page, nav entry, Ask Forge AI buttons |

chunks.title: Forge AI deployment
chunks.heading: Forge AI deployment — Before deploying
chunks.text:
1. Rebuild the generated files if `docs/` or `src/lib/neris/validation.js` changed since the last build:

   ```bash
   npm run build:forge-ai
   ```

2. Run the full test suite:

   ```bash
   npm test
   ```

3. Confirm the secret exists (it does if the AI Narrative Writer works). Don't print its value.

chunks.title: Forge AI deployment
chunks.heading: Forge AI deployment — Deploying
chunks.text:
Deploy rules and functions together, so the new callables never run against old rules:

```bash
firebase deploy --only functions,firestore:rules,hosting --project rms-dashboard-7562e --non-interactive
```

Never use `--force`. Deploying only the new functions is also fine:

```bash
firebase deploy --only functions:forgeAiBootstrap,functions:forgeAiAsk,functions:forgeAiListConversations,functions:forgeAiGetConversation,functions:forgeAiRenameConversation,functions:forgeAiArchiveConversation,functions:forgeAiFeedback,functions:forgeAiGetSettings,functions:forgeAiSaveSettings,functions:forgeAiUsageReport --project rms-dashboard-7562e --non-interactive
```

chunks.title: Forge AI deployment
chunks.heading: Forge AI deployment — After deploying
chunks.text:
1. Forge AI is off for every department. Turn it on per department in **Forge AI → Admin** (see [FORGE_AI_CONFIGURATION.md](FORGE_AI_CONFIGURATION.md)).
2. Grant the Forge AI permissions to custom roles where needed.
3. Ask one question per capability and check the answers cite real records.

chunks.title: Forge AI deployment
chunks.heading: Forge AI deployment — Rolling back
chunks.text:
- **Fastest:** turn Forge AI off for the department. Questions stop immediately; nothing else in FORGE depends on Forge AI.
- **Full:** redeploy the previous release. The Forge AI collections stay in Firestore and can be deleted later if wanted.

chunks.title: Forge AI deployment
chunks.heading: Forge AI deployment — Offline demo
chunks.text: `npm run demo:offline` seeds Forge AI as on for the `forge-demo` department. The emulator has no API key, so every answer is built from the records and labelled **From records (no AI model)**.

chunks.title: Forge AI known limitations
chunks.heading: Forge AI known limitations
chunks.text: Forge AI only answers from data FORGE already holds. Where that data doesn't exist, Forge AI says so in the answer's **Data limitations** section instead of guessing.

chunks.title: Forge AI known limitations
chunks.heading: Forge AI known limitations — Data that doesn't exist yet
chunks.text:
| Area | Limitation | What Forge AI does instead |
|---|---|---|
| Live CAD feed | FORGE has no live CAD or dispatch feed. | Dispatch Intelligence uses the CAD times recorded on NERIS reports, plus the Active911 alert window. Calls without a report don't appear. |
| Unit locations (AVL) | No live unit positions. | Unit answers use fleet status and the units recorded on reports. |
| Staffing | No live staffing or shift roster data. | Briefings leave staffing out and say so. |
| Active911 history | Active911 alerts are a rolling window, not a full history. | Alerts are labelled live with their sync time; older alerts aren't available. |
| Heat Zone | Calls without a location can't be placed in a district. Heat Zone also follows the member's Heat Zone district and history permissions. | Heat Zone answers say how many calls had no location and which permissions limited the answer. |

chunks.title: Forge AI known limitations
chunks.heading: Forge AI known limitations — Behaviour
chunks.text:
- **Answers aren't streamed.** A question shows "Reading records…" until the whole answer is ready (usually a few seconds, up to about a minute for briefings).
- **Report limit.** Each question reads at most the department's most recent 20,000 NERIS reports. Answers say when this limit was reached.
- **Keyword search for documentation.** Platform Knowledge uses keyword matching, not semantic search. Questions worded very differently from the docs may get "not documented" answers.
- **Questions are read by pattern, not free-form queries.** Time windows, unit names, report numbers, categories and addresses are picked out of the question. Unusual wording may fall back to the default window, which is always shown on the answer.
- **Response-time statistics** need at least 5 reports with response times; otherwise the briefing leaves the section out.
- **No write actions.** Forge AI never changes records. Fixes it suggests must be made in the relevant page.
- **Daily limit** is per department, not per member.
- **Model fallback.** When the model is unavailable or its answer fails validation, the answer is built from the records alone. It is accurate but less fluent, and has no AI observations.
- **Not a medical or legal tool.** Forge AI removes medication doses from answers and does not give medical direction, legal advice or findings about members.
- **Model answers can still be wrong.** Answers cite their sources and are validated, but members should check important facts against the records.

chunks.title: Forge AI permission matrix
chunks.heading: Forge AI permission matrix
chunks.text:
Forge AI adds five permissions. They are set per role in **System Admin → Roles & permissions** (group "Forge AI") and can be granted to individual members like any other permission.

| Permission | Label | What it allows |
|---|---|---|
| `useForgeAi` | Use Forge AI | Open Forge AI and ask questions |
| `useForgeAiBriefings` | Generate Forge AI briefings | Shift & Command Briefings |
| `useForgeAiSupervisorQa` | Forge AI supervisor QA | Supervisor QA reviews |
| `manageForgeAi` | Turn Forge AI on or off | Department settings (on/off, capabilities, daily limit) |
| `viewForgeAiUsage` | View Forge AI usage | Usage, feedback and audit tab (`manageForgeAi` includes this) |

chunks.title: Forge AI permission matrix
chunks.heading: Forge AI permission matrix — Default roles
chunks.text:
| Role | Use | Briefings | Supervisor QA | Manage | View usage |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Platform creator | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Fire Chief | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Battalion Chief | Yes | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| Company Officer | Yes | Yes | No | No | No |
| Firefighter | No | No | No | No | No |
| Read-only | No | No | No | No | No |
| IT Admin | Yes | No | No | Yes | Yes |

chunks.title: Forge AI permission matrix
chunks.heading: Forge AI permission matrix — Capability access
chunks.text:
A capability works only when **all** of these are true:

1. Forge AI is on for the department.
2. The capability is not switched off in Forge AI settings.
3. The department has the module the capability reads from.
4. The member has `useForgeAi` (platform creators always pass this step).
5. The member has the capability's data permissions.

| Capability | Data permissions | Module |
|---|---|---|
| Incident Intelligence | `viewNerisReports` | NERIS Fire Reports |
| Dispatch Intelligence | `viewNerisReports` | NERIS Fire Reports |
| Heat Zone Intelligence | `viewHeatZoneAnalytics` | Analytics |
| Unit & Resource Intelligence | `viewApparatus` or `viewFleetDashboard` | Apparatus |
| Shift & Command Briefings | `useForgeAiBriefings` and `viewNerisReports` | NERIS Fire Reports |
| NERIS Data Quality | `viewNerisReports` | NERIS Fire Reports |
| Supervisor QA | `useForgeAiSupervisorQa` and `viewNerisReports` | NERIS Fire Reports |
| Platform Knowledge | none beyond `useForgeAi` | none |

Briefings include the District, Geographic and Unit sections only when the member can also use Heat Zone Intelligence or Unit & Resource Intelligence. Heat Zone answers are further limited by the member's Heat Zone station or district scope, the same as the Heat Zone page.

chunks.title: Forge AI permission matrix
chunks.heading: Forge AI permission matrix — Stored data
chunks.text:
| Collection (under `departments/{id}/`) | Who can read it | Who writes it |
|---|---|---|
| `forgeAiConversations`, `forgeAiMessages`, `forgeAiMessageSources` | Only the member who owns the conversation, with `useForgeAi` | Cloud Functions only |
| `forgeAiBriefings` | Only the author, with `useForgeAiBriefings` | Cloud Functions only |
| `forgeAiSettings` | Through the `forgeAiGetSettings` function (`viewForgeAiUsage` or `manageForgeAi`) | `forgeAiSaveSettings` (`manageForgeAi`) |
| `forgeAiUsage`, `forgeAiUsageLogs`, `forgeAiFeedback` | Through `forgeAiUsageReport` (`viewForgeAiUsage` or `manageForgeAi`) | Cloud Functions only |

No member can read another department's Forge AI data. Browsers cannot write any Forge AI collection directly.

chunks.title: Forge AI user guide
chunks.heading: Forge AI user guide
chunks.text: Forge AI ("Public Safety Operations Intelligence") is a read-only assistant inside FORGE Responder. It answers questions from your department's own records and from FORGE's documentation. It never changes, submits or deletes anything.

chunks.title: Forge AI user guide
chunks.heading: Forge AI user guide — Opening Forge AI
chunks.text:
- Choose **Forge AI** in the left navigation, under Dashboard.
- Or use an **Ask Forge AI** button on another page. The button opens Forge AI with a question ready for that page:
  - **Command Dashboard**: "Shift briefing" writes a briefing for the last 24 hours.
  - **NERIS Fire Reports**: "Ask about calls" lists calls from the last 24 hours.
  - **NERIS report editor**: "Check with Forge AI" checks the saved report against Forge's NERIS rules.
  - **Heat Zone Analytics**: asks about districts and busy hours for the last 30 days.
  - **NERIS Analytics (Reporting)**: summarizes incidents this month.
  - **System Admin**: "Forge AI settings" opens the Forge AI admin tab.

The buttons only appear for members who can use Forge AI. If Forge AI is off or unavailable, the rest of FORGE keeps working as normal.

chunks.title: Forge AI user guide
chunks.heading: Forge AI user guide — What you can ask
chunks.text:
Forge AI picks a capability from your question, or you can choose one with the chips above the question box.

| Capability | Ask about | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Incident Intelligence | Incident summaries, timelines, missing fields, similar incidents | "Summarize incidents from the last 7 days" |
| Dispatch Intelligence | Calls by time, type, unit or address | "What calls did E1 run yesterday?" |
| Heat Zone Intelligence | Busy districts, repeat locations, hours of day, period comparison | "Which district was busiest in the last 30 days?" |
| Unit & Resource Intelligence | Fleet readiness, restrictions, unit activity | "Which units are out of service?" |
| Shift & Command Briefings | A structured briefing for a shift, week or month | "Create a shift briefing for the last 24 hours" |
| NERIS Data Quality | Missing or invalid NERIS fields | "Which draft reports are missing required fields?" |
| Supervisor QA | Rule failures, potential issues and observations for review | "Run a QA review for last week" |
| Platform Knowledge | How FORGE Responder works | "How do I turn on Heat Zone Analytics?" |

Time words Forge AI understands include: today, yesterday, last 24 hours, this shift, last N hours, last N days, last N weeks, this week, last week, this month, last month, this year, last year, month names, and dates such as 2026-03-01. Unit names such as "Engine 1", "E-1" and "E1" are treated the same. Without a time word, Forge AI uses a sensible default window and shows it on the answer.

chunks.title: Forge AI user guide
chunks.heading: Forge AI user guide — Reading an answer
chunks.text:
- **AI-written from records** means the AI model wrote the answer from the records listed under Sources.
- **From records (no AI model)** means Forge AI built the answer directly from the records, for example when the AI model isn't configured or didn't respond.
- **Access check** means Forge AI explained why it can't answer (for example, a missing permission).
- Citations such as [S1] point to the sources listed under the answer. Select a source to open the record.
- **Live** data (Active911 alerts, fleet status) shows when it was last updated. **Historical** data comes from saved reports. **Reference** sources are FORGE documentation.
- **AI observation** marks text the model wrote as an observation, not a fact from a record.
- **Data limitations** lists what the answer could not cover, such as the lack of a live CAD feed.
- Use the copy button to copy an answer, and the thumbs buttons to rate it.

Always check important facts against the source records. Forge AI does not explain why something happened, assign fault, or recommend discipline.

chunks.title: Forge AI user guide
chunks.heading: Forge AI user guide — Conversations
chunks.text: Your conversations are private to you. Use **New conversation** to start again, and rename or archive conversations from the history list. Archived conversations no longer show in the list.

chunks.title: Forge AI user guide
chunks.heading: Forge AI user guide — What Forge AI will not do
chunks.text:
- Change, submit, approve or delete records.
- Show you data you couldn't already open in FORGE.
- Read another department's data.
- Give medication doses or medical direction.
- Name civilians involved in incidents.
- Make findings about a member's fault or conduct.
- Describe features FORGE doesn't have.

chunks.title: Heat Zone Analytics — API
chunks.heading: Heat Zone Analytics — API
chunks.text:
All endpoints are Firebase **callable** Cloud Functions (`onCall`, region us-central1) defined in
`functions/index.js` with logic in `functions/lib/heatZone/service.js`. Client wrappers:
`src/lib/heatZone/heatZoneService.js`.

chunks.title: Heat Zone Analytics — API
chunks.heading: Heat Zone Analytics — API — Common behaviour
chunks.text:
* **Authentication:** Firebase Auth required (`unauthenticated` otherwise).
* **Tenant:** every request carries `departmentId`. It only *selects* the department; the server
  verifies an active membership (`departments/{d}/users/{uid}`, `status: "active"`), an active
  subscription, and the permission keys below. A forged or foreign `departmentId` is rejected with
  `permission-denied` exactly like any non-member.
* **Module gate:** if `platformEntitlements/{d}.modules` exists and lacks `analytics` → `permission-denied`.
* **District scope:** members without `viewHeatZoneAllDistricts` (or `manageHeatZoneSettings`) only
  receive incidents in the districts assigned to them in `heatZoneAccess/{uid}`. No assignment = no data.
* **History:** without `viewHeatZoneHistory`, date ranges are clamped to the last 30 days
  (department-local) and comparisons are omitted; `filters.historyLimited` is `true` in responses.
* **Errors:** `HttpsError` codes `unauthenticated`, `invalid-argument`, `permission-denied`,
  `not-found`, `failed-precondition`. Messages are plain English, safe to show.

chunks.title: Heat Zone Analytics — API
chunks.heading: Heat Zone Analytics — API — Filters object (request)
chunks.text:
```jsonc
{
  "from": "2026-10-01",          // department-local dates, inclusive. Default: last 30 days
  "to": "2026-10-31",
  "daysOfWeek": [1, 2, 3],       // 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday
  "timeStart": "22:00",          // HH:MM, department-local. start > end crosses midnight
  "timeEnd": "02:00",            //   (22:00–02:00 = 22:00–23:59 and 00:00–01:59)
  "districtIds": ["north-ab12c"],// "unassigned" = outside every configured district
  "zoneIds": [],                 // response zones
  "classifications": ["Fire"], "priorities": ["Emergency"], "dispositions": [], "statuses": [], "unitTypes": ["Engine"],
  "bounds": { "south": 32.3, "west": -89.5, "north": 32.4, "east": -89.4 } // geographic filter (applies to all stats)
}
```
Ranges are limited to 3 years. The server returns the normalised filters it actually applied.

| `heatZoneMarkers` | + `viewHeatZoneMarkers` + `viewNerisReports` | Clustered or paged incident markers for a viewport |
| `heatZoneIncident` | + `viewHeatZoneMarkers` + `viewNerisReports` | One incident's authorized detail (audited) |
| `heatZoneBoundaries` | `viewHeatZoneAnalytics` | District / response-zone geometry for the map |
| `heatZoneReport` | + `exportHeatZoneReports` (`comparison` also needs `viewHeatZoneHistory`) | Report data for CSV / XLSX / PDF (audited) |
| `heatZoneGetSettings` | + `manageHeatZoneSettings` | Zones, weights, member district assignments |
| `heatZoneSaveZones` | + `manageHeatZoneSettings` | Create/update a boundary or import GeoJSON; recalculates history |
| `heatZoneDeleteZone` | + `manageHeatZoneSettings` | Delete a boundary; recalculates history |
| `heatZoneSaveSettings` | + `manageHeatZoneSettings` | Priority weights, high-priority list |
| `heatZoneSetDistrictAccess` | + `manageHeatZoneSettings` | Assign districts to a member |
| `heatZoneRebuild` | + `manageHeatZoneSettings` | Recalculate every projection from the source reports |
| `heatZoneSaveGeocoding` | + `manageHeatZoneSettings` | Turn address geocoding on or off; recalculates |

chunks.heading: Heat Zone Analytics — API — heatZoneMarkers
chunks.text:
Request: `{ departmentId, filters, viewport: {south, west, north, east}, zoom, page?: 0, pageSize?: 200 (max 400) }`

Response when zoomed out (zoom < 14) with more than 60 visible incidents:
`{ "mode": "clusters", "total": 812, "clusters": [{ "lat", "lng", "count" }] }`

Otherwise: `{ "mode": "markers", "total", "page", "pageSize", "hasMore",

chunks.title: Heat Zone Analytics — API
chunks.heading: Heat Zone Analytics — API — heatZoneIncident
chunks.text:
Request: `{ departmentId, id }` (marker id). Response: `{ id, reportNumber, occurredAt, localDate, timeZone,
address, lat, lng, classification, classificationDetail, priority, disposition, status, units[], unitTypes[],
stations[], responseSeconds, district: {id, name}, zones: [{id, name}] }`. Returns `not-found` for an id
outside the caller's department or district scope (no existence leak). Writes an audit log entry.

chunks.title: Heat Zone Analytics — API
chunks.heading: Heat Zone Analytics — API — heatZoneBoundaries
chunks.text:
Request: `{ departmentId }` → `{ zones: [{ id, name, kind, color, active, bbox: [s, w, n, e], geometry }] }`
(GeoJSON Polygon/MultiPolygon). Districts outside a restricted caller's scope are omitted.

chunks.title: Heat Zone Analytics — API
chunks.heading: Heat Zone Analytics — API — heatZoneReport
chunks.text:
Request: `{ departmentId, reportType: "geographic" | "district" | "hourly" | "daily" | "classification" | "comparison", filters, format: "csv" | "xlsx" | "pdf" }`

Response: `{ meta: { agencyName, departmentId, reportType, title, format, from, to, timeZone, filters: string[],
districtScope, totalCalls, generatedAt, generatedAtLocal, generatedBy, truncated }, columns: string[], rows: any[][], notes: string[] }`.
The browser renders CSV / XLSX (SheetJS) / printable PDF from this payload (`src/lib/heatZone/heatZoneExport.js`).
Each call writes `departments/{d}/auditLogs` (`action: "heat_zone_report_exported"`).

chunks.title: Heat Zone Analytics — API
chunks.heading: Heat Zone Analytics — API — Settings callables
chunks.text:
* `heatZoneGetSettings { departmentId }` → `{ settings, timeZone, zones: [{id, name, kind, color, priority, active, bbox}], members: [{uid, email, name, role, districtIds}], meta }`
* `heatZoneSaveZones { departmentId, zone: { id?, name, kind, color?, priority?, active?, geometry | geoJson } }`
  or `{ departmentId, geoJson, kind, nameProperty? }` (FeatureCollection import, ≤ 200 features) →
  `{ saved: [{id, name}], rebuild: { projected, written, removed, skipped, rejected } }`
* `heatZoneDeleteZone { departmentId, zoneId }` → `{ deleted, rebuild }`
* `heatZoneSaveSettings { departmentId, settings: { priorityWeights: {Emergency: 3, …}, highPriorities: ["Emergency"] } }`
* `heatZoneSetDistrictAccess { departmentId, uid, districtIds: [] }` (ids must be existing districts or `"unassigned"`)
* `heatZoneRebuild { departmentId }` → `{ projected, written, removed, skipped, rejected, geocoding }`.
  `geocoding` = `{ enabled, googleConfigured, addresses, stored, lookedUp, found, notFound, imprecise, failed, waiting }`.
  At most 300 new addresses are looked up per recalculation; `waiting` says how many are left.
* `heatZoneSaveGeocoding { departmentId, enabled: boolean }` → `{ enabled, rebuild }`. Turning it on
  needs a Google Geocoding (or Maps JS) key in the department's Google APIs integration
  (`failed-precondition` otherwise). Audited as `heat_zone_geocoding_changed`.
* `heatZoneGetSettings` also returns `geocoding: { enabled, googleConfigured, geocodedAddresses }`.

chunks.title: Heat Zone Analytics — API
chunks.heading: Heat Zone Analytics — API — Live updates
chunks.text:
`departments/{d}/heatZoneMeta/state` holds `{ version, zonesVersion, updatedAt, lastChange }`. The
browser listens with `onSnapshot` (`watchHeatZoneVersion`), which Firestore rules allow only for
members of that department with `viewHeatZoneAnalytics`. When `version` changes the page refetches.

chunks.title: Heat Zone Analytics — API
chunks.heading: Heat Zone Analytics — API — Triggers (not callable)
chunks.text:
* `heatZoneOnReportItem` — `departments/{d}/lists/hlfd-rms-neris-fire-reports/items/{itemId}` (`retry: true`)
* `heatZoneOnReportList` — `departments/{d}/lists/hlfd-rms-neris-fire-reports` (legacy array storage)

chunks.title: Heat Zone Analytics — Database Schema
chunks.heading: Heat Zone Analytics — Database Schema
chunks.text:
Database: **Cloud Firestore** (the platform's only database). All collections are tenant-scoped under

chunks.heading: Heat Zone Analytics — Database Schema — Source of truth (unchanged)
chunks.text:
`departments/{d}/lists/hlfd-rms-neris-fire-reports` — NERIS incident reports, either

every projection maps 1:1 to a source record and can be deleted/rebuilt at any time.

| Field | Type | Source / rule |

| `departmentId` | string | Path department (re-checked on every read) |
| `sourceId`, `source` | string | `report.id`, `"hlfd-rms-neris-fire-reports"` |
| `reportNumber` | string | `reportNumber` → `workspace.cad.incidentNumber` → `cadCallNumber` |
| `occurredAt` | number (UTC ms) | `cad.receivedTime` → `cad.dispatchTime` → earliest unit dispatch → `incidentDate` (local midnight). Wall-clock values are read in the department time zone |
| `localDate`, `localMonth`, `localHour`, `localMinute`, `localDow` | string/number | `occurredAt` in the department zone (Sun = 0) |
| `timeZone` | string | `profile/main.timezone` at projection time |

| `status` | string | Report workflow status (Draft … Submitted) — the only status the platform has |
| `unitTypes[]`,

chunks.title: Heat Zone Analytics — Database Schema
chunks.heading: Heat Zone Analytics — Database Schema — `heatZoneGeocodes/{key}` — geocoded report addresses (server-only)
chunks.text:
One entry per normalised address query; `key` is a SHA-256 of the lower-cased query (32 hex chars).
`{ query, status: "ok" | "not_found" | "imprecise", lat?, lng?, locationType?, formattedAddress?,
geocodedAt, retryAfter? (not_found only, +30 days), departmentId }`.

* The query is `incidentAddress`, completed with the profile's `city`, `stateId` and `zip` when it has no comma.
* Only Google `ROOFTOP`, `RANGE_INTERPOLATED` and `GEOMETRIC_CENTER` results are used. `APPROXIMATE`
  (town or postcode level) and partial matches are stored as `imprecise` and never mapped.
* Network, quota and key errors are **not** stored, so the address is retried on the next write or
  recalculation.
* Geocodes are **never written into the NERIS report**. The report stays the authoritative record that
  members edit and that is submitted to NERIS.
* Projections gain `locationSource`: `"report"` (coordinates on the report, which always win),
  `"geocoded"` or `""` (not mapped).

chunks.title: Heat Zone Analytics — Database Schema
chunks.heading: Heat Zone Analytics — Database Schema — Historical recalculation
chunks.text:
* Any report change → that projection is recomputed from the **current** source record.
* Boundary create/update/delete → `zonesVersion` bump + full department rebuild (district assignment
  of past calls changes).
* Time-zone change in the department profile → run `heatZoneRebuild` (Settings → Recalculate) or the
  backfill script; see known-limitations.md.

chunks.heading: Heat Zone Analytics — Deployment Guide — Order of deployment (staging first, then production)
chunks.text:
The new rules only *add* collections, and the new functions only *read* existing data, so deploying
in this order never breaks the running app.

1. **Rules + indexes / TTL policy**
   ```bash
   firebase deploy --only firestore:rules,firestore:indexes --project staging
   ```
   `firestore.indexes.json` adds a TTL policy on `heatZoneEvents.expireAt` and an index exemption on
   `heatZoneZones.geometryJson`. TTL policies can take a while to become active; nothing depends on it.

2. **Functions** (triggers + callables)
   ```bash
   firebase deploy --only functions:heatZoneOnReportItem,functions:heatZoneOnReportList,functions:heatZoneDashboard,functions:heatZoneMarkers,functions:heatZoneIncident,functions:heatZoneBoundaries,functions:heatZoneReport,functions:heatZoneGetSettings,functions:heatZoneSaveZones,functions:heatZoneDeleteZone,functions:heatZoneSaveSettings,functions:heatZoneSetDistrictAccess,functions:heatZoneRebuild,functions:heatZoneSaveGeocoding --project staging
   ```
   (Or `npm run deploy:staging`, which deploys everything.)

3. **Data migration (backfill)** — builds projections for existing reports. Dry run first:
   ```bash
   npm run backfill:heat-zone
   ```
   then apply (PowerShell; set the target project first):
   ```bash
   npm run backfill:heat-zone:apply
   ```
   Uses Application Default Credentials and `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`. Safe to re-run.

4. **Member grants** — the rules check `memberGrants` for the live-update listener. Existing members'
   grants refresh when their membership or role changes; to refresh everyone now:
   ```bash
   npm run backfill:memberships
   ```
   or `node scripts/sync-member-grants.mjs --apply` with `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` set.

chunks.title: Heat Zone Analytics — Known Limitations
chunks.heading: Heat Zone Analytics — Known Limitations — Data availability (platform gaps, not module bugs)
chunks.text:
1. **No CAD calls-for-service archive.** The module analyses NERIS incident reports, the only
   authoritative incident records. Calls that never become a NERIS report are not counted.
   Active911 alerts keep no history (rolling 25 alerts) and are not used.
2. **Coordinates.** Reports created in the editor have no latitude/longitude input; CAD imports and
   demo data carry coordinates. With **Settings → Address geocoding** turned on (needs the department's
   Google Geocoding key), reports without coordinates are placed from their incident address. Calls that
   are still unmapped are counted in every statistic and chart, shown as "N not mapped", and excluded
   from the map and geographic bounds.
   * Addresses that only match a town or ZIP code are deliberately not mapped.
   * Each recalculation looks up at most 300 new addresses; run it again for larger backlogs. New
     reports are looked up as they are saved.
   * Geocoding uses the department's Google quota and sends incident addresses to Google, so it is off
     by default.
   * There is no manual pin placement for addresses Google can't find.
3. **No incident disposition or call status fields.** Disposition is derived (see database-schema.md);
   "status" is the NERIS report workflow status.
4. **No districts / beats existed.** Boundaries must be uploaded per department (GeoJSON). Until then,
   every call is "Outside configured districts" and district-restricted members see nothing.
   "Patrol zone" is presented as **Response zone** (fire/EMS terminology).
5. **Response time** is dispatch → first arrival and is shown only when ≥ 5 incidents in the selection
   have both times.

chunks.title: Heat Zone Analytics — Known Limitations
chunks.heading: Heat Zone Analytics — Known Limitations — Technical limits
chunks.text:
6. **Firestore instead of PostGIS.** Spatial work (point-in-polygon, grid binning, clustering) runs in
   Cloud Functions. Queries read every projection in the date range (cap **50 000** per request;
   responses flag `truncated`). Very large multi-year ranges for large agencies should use narrower
   ranges or a future pre-aggregated rollup.
7. **Cache is per function instance** (no shared Redis). Correctness is unaffected (version-keyed);
   hit rate is lower under autoscaling.
8. **Live-update contention.** Every analytics change increments one `heatZoneMeta/state` document
   inside the projection transaction (Firestore sustains ~1 write/s per document comfortably).
   Bulk imports of hundreds of reports at once will retry transactions and take longer to settle.
9. **Time-zone change.** If a department changes `profile.timezone`, existing projections keep the old
   local hour/date until **Settings → Recalculate analytics** (or the backfill script) is run.
10. **Custom roles** keep their stored permissions; Heat Zone keys must be granted to them manually.
    Existing members' rule grants refresh on their next membership/role change or via
    `scripts/sync-member-grants.mjs --apply`.
11. **PDF export** uses the browser print dialog ("Save as PDF"), matching the existing hydrant reports;
    there is no server-generated PDF.
12. **Heat map rendering** is a custom canvas layer over server-binned cells (~24 px). It is a density
    visualisation, not a kernel-density estimate.
13. **Offline / field app**: not included (desktop and tablet RMS only).

chunks.title: Heat Zone Analytics — Known Limitations
chunks.heading: Heat Zone Analytics — Known Limitations — Minor UI gaps
chunks.text:
14. Priority weights can be edited but a custom priority can't be removed from the weight list.
15. Without the history permission, a date range older than 30 days stays selected in the filter bar;

16. "Today" in presets is computed when the page loads and goes stale if the page is left open overnight.
17. Zone priority (which district wins where boundaries overlap) is stored but not editable in the UI;

18. Marker and incident detail access also need the existing `viewNerisReports` permission (deliberate:

chunks.title: Heat Zone Analytics — Tenant Security
chunks.heading: Heat Zone Analytics — Tenant Security
chunks.text:
Tenant = department. Isolation is enforced in four independent layers; any one of them alone blocks
cross-department access.

chunks.title: Heat Zone Analytics — Tenant Security
chunks.heading: Heat Zone Analytics — Tenant Security — 1. Server-side identity and tenant verification
chunks.text:
* Every callable runs `resolveCaller()` (`functions/lib/heatZone/service.js`):
  1. Firebase Auth uid required.
  2. `departmentId` from the request is validated as an id and treated as a **selector only**.
  3. `assertMemberPermission()` (existing `functions/lib/access.js`) requires an *active* membership
     doc `departments/{d}/users/{uid}`, an active subscription/department, and the
     `viewHeatZoneAnalytics` permission computed from the member's roles + overrides
     (`functions/lib/memberGrants.js`). Platform creators (`platformCreators/{uid}`) pass.
  4. Module entitlement `analytics` checked against `platformEntitlements/{d}`.
  5. District scope loaded from `heatZoneAccess/{uid}` unless the member may view all districts.
* A forged `departmentId` therefore fails exactly like a non-member (`permission-denied`).
* Triggers never take a tenant from data: the department comes from the document **path**
  (`departments/{departmentId}/lists/...`). A source record whose own `departmentId` field names a
  different department is **rejected** (not projected anywhere) and logged.

chunks.title: Heat Zone Analytics — Tenant Security
chunks.heading: Heat Zone Analytics — Tenant Security — 2. Tenant-scoped storage and queries
chunks.text:
* All Heat Zone data lives under `departments/{d}/…`; every query is built from the verified
  department path (`heatZoneCalls` collection of that department only).
* Defence in depth: rows whose stored `departmentId` differs from the verified department are dropped
  at read time; incident lookups re-check it.
* Geographic queries are filters over the tenant's own rows. Two departments with identical
  coordinates are tested to prove proximity never mixes data.

chunks.title: Heat Zone Analytics — Tenant Security
chunks.heading: Heat Zone Analytics — Tenant Security — 3. Database-level row security (Firestore rules)
chunks.text:
| Collection | Browser read | Browser write |
|---|---|---|
| `heatZoneMeta/state` | members of **that** department with `viewHeatZoneAnalytics` (`memberCanAny`) | never |
| `heatZoneCalls`, `heatZoneZones`, `heatZoneSettings`, `heatZoneAccess`, `heatZoneEvents`, `heatZoneGeocodes` | never | never |

All seven are listed in `hasExplicitTenantRule()` so the tenant catch-all rule cannot widen them.
Analytics are only reachable through the callables, which apply district scope — something rules
alone could not express for aggregates.

chunks.title: Heat Zone Analytics — Tenant Security
chunks.heading: Heat Zone Analytics — Tenant Security — 4. Tenant-specific caching, jobs, subscriptions and reports
chunks.text:
* **Cache** (`functions/lib/heatZone/cache.js`): per-instance LRU. Key =
  `departmentId | data version | caller district scope | hash(filters, zoom, mode, capabilities)`.
  A key cannot be built without a department id; data changes bump the version so stale entries are
  unreachable; restricted members never share entries with broader scopes.
* **Background processing**: triggers and rebuilds are per department; the event ledger is
  per department (`departments/{d}/heatZoneEvents`).
* **Real-time**: browsers subscribe only to `departments/{d}/heatZoneMeta/state`, permitted by rules
  per department; the doc carries a counter, not data. Fresh data always comes from an authorized callable.
* **Reports/exports**: generated server-side under the same `resolveCaller()` checks plus
  `exportHeatZoneReports`; contents respect district scope; each export is written to that
  department's `auditLogs`.

chunks.title: Heat Zone Analytics — Tenant Security
chunks.heading: Heat Zone Analytics — Tenant Security — Address geocoding
chunks.text:
* Each department's addresses are looked up only with **its own** Google key, read on the server from
  `departments/{d}/integrations/googleApis`. The key never reaches the browser.
* Results are stored under that department (`heatZoneGeocodes`) and are never read for another
  department, even for the same address. This is tested with two departments sharing an address.
* A report claiming another department's id is rejected before any lookup, so it is never sent to Google.
* Geocoding is off by default. Only `manageHeatZoneSettings` can turn it on, and the change is audited.

| `viewHeatZoneAnalytics` | Open the module, dashboard, heat map | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | – |

chunks.title: Offline demo (no Wi-Fi)
chunks.heading: Offline demo (no Wi-Fi)
chunks.text:
The whole FORGE Responder platform runs on this laptop with no internet: the RMS
(every module), FORGE FIELD and the Creator Console. It uses local copies of
Firebase (sign-in, database, file storage and the server functions), so nothing
touches production.

chunks.title: Offline demo (no Wi-Fi)
chunks.heading: Offline demo (no Wi-Fi) — Start
chunks.text:
```bash
npm run demo:offline
```

The first run builds the app (about a minute). After that it starts in about
20 seconds and opens the browser at `http://localhost:4173/demo`. Click
**Launch Demo RMS** as usual.

- **FORGE FIELD:** `http://localhost:4173/field` (after launching the demo).
- **Creator Console:** `http://localhost:4173/creator-console`. The login is in
  `.offline-demo/creator-login.txt` (made on first run; works on this laptop only).

Stop with **Ctrl+C** in that window. Changes you make during a demo are kept
for next time (also saved every 5 minutes).

chunks.title: Offline demo (no Wi-Fi)
chunks.heading: Offline demo (no Wi-Fi) — Before demo day (with internet)
chunks.text:
1. Pull the latest code, then rebuild the offline copy:
   `npm run demo:offline -- --rebuild`
2. Click through once. Open a hydrant map in FORGE FIELD while online so the
   map imagery for the area is saved on the laptop.
3. Stop with Ctrl+C. Optionally turn Wi-Fi off and start again to rehearse.

Start over with fresh sample data: `npm run demo:offline -- --reset`.

chunks.title: Offline demo (no Wi-Fi)
chunks.heading: Offline demo (no Wi-Fi) — Another computer (jump drive)
chunks.text:
Stop the demo, plug in the drive, then:

```bash
npm run demo:usb -- D:\
```

This writes `D:\FORGE-Demo.zip` (about 500 MB) and a read-me. The zip holds the
app, its packages, the saved demo data, the Firebase emulator files and portable
Node and Java, so the other Windows computer needs no installs and no internet.
On that computer: copy the zip to the Desktop, Extract All, and double-click
**Start FORGE Demo.cmd**. Run `demo:usb` again after code changes or new demo
data.

- The Inter web font (the app falls back to Segoe UI; it looks nearly the same).
